Triage: lands in `domain:devx` (`vitest.config.mts`, root test config); rationale: admitted under class (a), and the admission turns on **where** the false sentence lives. This is not a source comment — it is the text of a `throw`, i.e. output an operator or agent reads at the moment they are blocked. That is the same shape this repo already admits and graded on #7775 (a guard's refusal message advertising a remedy that cannot work). A refusal message is a contract with its reader; this one states *"this run would collect ZERO files and exit GREEN"* and the card falsifies it with a named probe — `pnpm exec vitest run --project @object-ui/does-not-exist` → `No projects matched the filter`, exit 1, captured before any pipe, on vitest 4.1.10. Probe named, claim falsified ⇒ `Bug`.

I want to be explicit that this seat nearly closed it, because the precedent matters more than the card. Earlier in this round I closed cards for "in-file prose contradicts in-file enforced truth" (objectui#8162, objectui#8270). This one is not that: those were prose no one is required to read at a decision point, and this is the string printed **into** the decision. The distinction is the grading line, and it is now written down rather than re-derived.

The measured cost is not hypothetical — it is recorded in the card's own provenance: the filing seat reached for the sentence while deciding whether a `--project`-based package script needed an empty-collection guard, could not trust it, and had to go measure. Believing it leads somewhere specific and wrong (every `--project` call site needs a name-validity guard) and away from the real silent case (a project that **does** resolve and globs zero files — different mechanism, different remedy, `--no-passWithNoTests`, as objectui#8240 used and PR objectui#8273 landed).

`priority:p3`: one file, one sentence, and the guard around it is sound and worth keeping — the card says so first and this seat agrees. ⛔ This is not a request to delete the guard; its value (naming the env var, explaining the `dist` lane needs a built package, pointing at `pnpm test:dist`) is independent of the stale premise.

Scope note for whoever takes it: only one of the two entangled claims is stale. ⛔ Do not touch *"the `dist` project is not declared unless `OBJECTUI_DIST_PINS` is `1`"* — that is still true. Whether to pin the vitest-version dependency with a test is optional; a re-worded justification alone closes the misinformation, and the card's "not verified which vitest version the sentence was true of" should stay unverified rather than be guessed at in the replacement text.

Carrier check: objectui#8240 closed `completed` at 07:58 today via merged PR objectui#8273, so ⛔ there is no live PR to carry this as an acceptance note — which is part of why it is a card rather than a rider.

⛔ This seat grades and routes only: not claimed, not dispatched, no code.

**The grading line triage drew is carried into the brief, because the PR should preserve it.** This seat's read of that reasoning: the same round closed cards where in-file PROSE contradicts in-file truth (#8162, #8270), and admitted this one because the false sentence is the text of a `throw` — output an operator or agent reads at the moment they are blocked. A refusal message is a contract with its reader, and the measured cost is in this card's own provenance: the filing seat reached for the sentence, could not trust it, and had to go measure vitest itself.

**Brief.** Re-derive the probe (`vitest run --project <nonexistent>`, exit code captured before any pipe) on today's installed vitest and report what it actually does — if the behaviour has moved again, both the card and the brief are stale and the dev's reading wins. ⛔ Do not delete the guard: its message names the env var, explains that the `dist` lane needs a built package, and points at `pnpm test:dist`, and that value is independent of the stale sentence. Rewrite only the justification so it states something true, decided under the four axes against one test — would a reader who trusts this sentence and acts on it be misled? Then sweep the tree for the same claim elsewhere and correct only what the dev's own probe proves false. Finally, decide whether a mechanical pin is warranted, with the trade stated: a pin that greps for a sentence is weak, one that runs the probe is strong but costs a vitest spawn.

**Known noise, named so it is not mistaken for this PR's:** `check:lint-rule-coverage` reds when a gitignored build artifact is present (#8369, filed today against the gate this lane landed this afternoon). Not this card's.

Closed by PR #8383, squash-merged into `main` at 2026-09-07T15:59:45Z as `c8ae7648a`. Verified on re-fetched `origin/main` (tip `c8ae7648a`, read 16:01Z), not on the report's narrative — full probe with its control is on the PR (`5573146670`).

**What this card actually bought.** The guard was never deleted and its remedy text is unchanged in substance: it still names `OBJECTUI_DIST_PINS`, still explains that the `dist` lane needs a built package, still points at `pnpm test:dist`. What changed is the *justification*: the sentence claiming the un-opted run would "collect ZERO files and exit GREEN" is gone from the message, replaced by what vitest measurably does — throw `No projects matched the filter "dist"` and exit 1. The guard's reason for existing is now the true one: vitest's refusal is loud but *unhelpful*, naming neither the env gate nor the remedy.

⭐ **The claim is now mechanically pinned, not merely corrected.** `scripts/__tests__/dist-pins-guard-message-8274.test.ts` (149 lines, 5 cases) spawns vitest for real, and it carries its own non-vacuity control so the negative assertions cannot pass against an empty slice. That is the difference between a comment that rots and a claim that reds — and it is why the residual `exit GREEN` strings on main are fine: every one of them is a quotation inside a negation of itself.

The `pm:*` state label is stripped in the same stroke; `domain:devx`, `tests` and `priority:p3` stay — attribution is not state.
